new ArrayBuffer().description:
new ArrayBuffer(byteLength[, options])
a fixed-length raw binary data buffer. Pass `{ maxByteLength }` in `options` to make it resizable (see `.resize()`).

ArrayBuffer.prototype.resize().description:
ES2024
buffer.resize(newByteLength)
grows or shrinks a resizable ArrayBuffer in place (must have been created with `{ maxByteLength }`), without reallocating or invalidating existing views.

ArrayBuffer.prototype.transfer().description:
ES2024
buffer.transfer([newByteLength])
moves the buffer's data to a new ArrayBuffer (optionally resizing) and detaches the original — `buffer.byteLength` becomes `0` and it can no longer be used. Cheap ownership transfer without a copy.

new Uint8Array().description:
new Uint8Array(length | typedArray | object | buffer[, byteOffset[, length]])
a typed array of 8-bit unsigned integers (0-255) — the most common TypedArray, used for raw byte data.

new Int32Array().description:
new Int32Array(length | typedArray | object | buffer[, byteOffset[, length]])
a typed array of 32-bit signed integers.

new Float64Array().description:
new Float64Array(length | typedArray | object | buffer[, byteOffset[, length]])
a typed array of 64-bit floating point numbers (standard JS `number` precision).

new Float16Array().description:
ES2025
new Float16Array(length | typedArray | object | buffer[, byteOffset[, length]])
a typed array of half-precision (16-bit) floating point numbers — half the memory of Float32Array, useful for ML/GPU-adjacent data.

Uint8Array.prototype.toBase64().description:
ES2026
bytes.toBase64([options])
return a base64-encoded string representation of the Uint8Array's bytes.

Uint8Array.fromBase64().description:
ES2026
Uint8Array.fromBase64(base64String[, options])
decode a base64 string into a new Uint8Array.

Uint8Array.prototype.toHex().description:
ES2026
bytes.toHex()
return a lowercase-hex-encoded string representation of the Uint8Array's bytes.

Uint8Array.fromHex().description:
ES2026
Uint8Array.fromHex(hexString)
decode a hex string into a new Uint8Array.

new DataView().description:
new DataView(buffer[, byteOffset[, byteLength]])
provides explicit, endianness-aware get/set methods (e.g. `getUint32(offset, littleEndian)`) for reading and writing arbitrary numeric types at any byte offset in an ArrayBuffer — use this instead of a TypedArray when the layout is mixed-type or externally defined (e.g. a binary file format).
